clue.text: Paltry cash prize

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
a pot is slang for a trophy cup, a prize won

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a measly cash award.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot describes something petty and inferior, which is what paltry means.

clue.text: Recapture bear on other side

parts.note: to bear is to take or carry
back means at the reverse side

explanation.surface: Seizing a bear again on the far side.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back territory is to regain or recapture it.

clue.text: A bishop in original story

indicators.note: the article and the bishop go inside the word for original

parts.note: native means original, belonging by birth
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop features in the original tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, a story.

clue.text: Antelope and steer crossing railway

indicators.note: the ox straddles the railway letters

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated bull, an ox

explanation.surface: An antelope and a bullock crossing the tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: The oryx is a large straight-horned African and Arabian antelope.

clue.text: Label's left inside for perfectionist

indicators.note: the label has the letter for left placed within it

parts.note: a sticker is a label; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A label has been left inside something, annoying a fussy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exactness in every detail, the mark of a perfectionist.

clue.text: Kew date rearranged, altered

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A Kew Gardens appointment has been moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweaked means adjusted slightly, altered.

clue.text: Female executive, one employed by daily

indicators.note: the digit is put to work inside the cleaner's title

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning woman who comes in each day
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman boss, someone hired by a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like a newspaper; it is the British word for a daily cleaner, a charwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairwoman is a woman presiding over a board, a senior executive.

clue.text: Learning about island in French river

indicators.note: the learning goes around the island's letter

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge

explanation.surface: Studying an island in a French river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is France's longest river, flowing to the Atlantic at Nantes.

clue.text: Outcome of Ulster broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: The result of a radio programme from Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is the outcome of an event.

clue.text: Fast female telling untruths

parts.note: lying means telling untruths

explanation.surface: A woman is quick to lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying can mean very swift, as in a flying visit.

clue.text: Terrier from Scottish island failing to keep head down

indicators.note: the islet word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a skerry is a small rocky islet, a word from Orkney and Shetland Norse
blue means sad, down in spirits

explanation.surface: A dog from the Hebrides that won't stay low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head down' reads as one phrase but splits: 'head' belongs to the deletion, 'down' is the sad sense. A skerry is a rocky islet off Scotland's coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kerry blue is an Irish terrier breed with a soft blue-grey coat.

clue.text: Sign changes, five having been driven out

indicators.note: says the letter for five is expelled from the verb

parts.note: to vary is to change, so varies means changes
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A sign alters after five have been ejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries is the Ram, the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Couple caught out leaving Scottish bank

indicators.note: signals the letter for caught is removed from the word for couple

parts.note: a brace is a pair or couple, as of game birds
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A pair caught out departing from a Scottish bank.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a brae is a hillside or steep bank, as of a river.

clue.text: Fairy ring located by gypsy

parts.note: tinker is an old word for a travelling gypsy
a bell rings, so ring can mean bell (give someone a bell = phone)

explanation.surface: A fairy ring has been found by a traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'located by' just puts the ring next to the gypsy, the gypsy first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinker Bell is the fairy companion of Peter Pan in Barrie's story.

clue.text: What may be termed "Glorious" on island reserve?

parts.note: the Glorious Twelfth is 12 August, the start of the British grouse-shooting season
the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Asking what may be called glorious on an island reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the twelfth man is the reserve fielder; the question mark marks this as a cricket sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket team's substitute fielder is its twelfth man.

clue.text: Natter in church with popular footballer's wife?

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
WAG, wives and girlfriends, a British tabloid label for footballers' partners

explanation.surface: Gossip in church with a well-liked footballer's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs are 'wives and girlfriends' of England footballers in British tabloid slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal chat, a natter.

clue.text: Rex brought in vodka cocktail for Czech composer

indicators.note: the king's letter is brought inside the mixed spirit
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of vodka are mixed

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is served a vodka cocktail in honour of a Czech composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes VODKA into DVOAK; 'brought in' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonín Dvořák was the Czech composer of the New World Symphony.

clue.text: Judges 24 different roses across the south

parts.note: 24-down's answer is a fool, which is an ass

indicators.note: the rearranged flowers stretch across the letter for south
the letters are made different, rearranged

parts.note: S abbreviates south

explanation.surface: Fools of all kinds take varied roses down south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges ROSES; 'across' puts S inside to give ESSORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessors evaluate and judge, as in court or for insurance.

clue.text: Check on board earlier vessel

indicators.note: goes inside the other piece, as a passenger is carried aboard

parts.note: sooner means earlier
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Inspect the boat before departure.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigging on two or more masts.

clue.text: Criminal blamed for state of uproar

indicators.note: something criminal is wrong or bent, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A criminal is blamed for a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named from the old London madhouse, means a scene of chaos and uproar.

clue.text: Most are blown for an eminent conductor

indicators.note: blown suggests being blown apart, scattering the letters

explanation.surface: Most are blown away by a great conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestro is an honorific for a distinguished conductor or musician.

clue.text: Remarkably typical Conservative girl in charge

parts.note: lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A Tory girl being in charge is remarkably typical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkably' qualifies the definition: something remarkably typical is a classic case.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic example is a perfectly representative one.

clue.text: Exclusive group in old golf club, reportedly

indicators.note: means the word is to be heard rather than seen

parts.note: a cleek is an old iron-headed golf club

explanation.surface: An elite set in an old golfing society, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' suggests a club of members; it is an old club for hitting the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is a small exclusive circle of people.

clue.text: Disturbance behind American

parts.note: rump is the backside, the behind
US means American

explanation.surface: A fuss behind an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy commotion or disturbance.

clue.text: 9? Undecided

definitions.meaning: the answer to 9-down, fast-moving through the sky, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unresolved, and literally describes something aloft and airborne.

clue.text: Fool's short turn of phrase, irritant ultimately

indicators.note: short means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: an idiom is a turn of phrase

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter

explanation.surface: A fool's abbreviated expression is an irritant in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a foolish, stupid person.

clue.text: Czechoslovakia's capital

indicators.note: the 's stands for 'has': the country name has the city within it

explanation.surface: A question about the capital of the old Czechoslovakia.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for Prague; the capital is in fact sitting inside the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Ruler has worked hard

indicators.note: worked means shaped or reworked, so the letters are moved

parts.note: H abbreviates hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A ruler has laboured hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shah was the title of the monarch of Iran.

clue.text: King of Troy married after pair split up

indicators.note: the letter for married comes after the shuffled pair
the pair are separated and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Trojan king weds after a couple separate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split up' signals the anagram; the surface pictures a couple separating, not letters being shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the last king of Troy, father of Hector and Paris.

clue.text: Try to land

definitions.meaning: in rugby a try is scored by grounding the ball over the line
for an aircraft, to come down on the ground

explanation.definitionFit: In American football a scoring grounding is named this, and an aircraft's landing is too.

clue.text: Take the place of model in favour of keeping home

indicators.note: the two pieces hold the word for home between them

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model
for means supporting, in favour of
in means at home

explanation.surface: A deputy model supports keeping the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit in for someone is to substitute for them temporarily.

clue.text: Frantic search for an engraver

indicators.note: frantic suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A desperate hunt for an engraver.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser engraves or embosses metal, chasing being decorative metalwork.
